generatedCommentsNodes.comment: The nested `assertBusy` pattern (outer 1-minute timeout wrapping an inner default 10-second timeout) is intentional per the Javadoc, but it means the total wall-clock time can exceed the outer timeout by up to the inner timeout (≈ 70 s in the worst case). More importantly, the inner `assertBusy` will exhaust its full 10-second retry budget on every outer iteration before the outer loop gets a chance to back off and retry. This makes the effective polling cadence coarser than the outer timeout suggests. Consider whether a single `assertBusy` with a 1-minute timeout and the hot-threads logging inside the lambda would achieve the same goal with simpler semantics and a tighter time bound.
